answer: Like a falcon that cannot be in two skies at once, each agent proves it occupies a distinct point on the network: independent observers measure round-trip latency from many vantage points, triangulating its location. A sybil farm running dozens of identities on one machine shows identical latency fingerprints, so the swarm is flagged before it can wander into the market and sip the nectar of shared rewards. Faking a new location means renting real machines in real places, which makes each extra identity genuinely expensive.
